claims.statement: Military power is a relational system joining political purpose, organized force, command, information, sustainment, friction, law, care, consequence, and memory.

On 26 February 1991 the U.S. Army's 2d Armored Cavalry Regiment, leading VII Corps, fought Iraqi forces associated with the Tawakalna and 12th Armored Divisions in the action later named the Battle of 73 Easting after a north-south map grid line.
claims.uncertainty: Official U.S. accounts are not the whole battle. Iraqi participant, civilian, regional, environmental, and independent scholarly sources remain required for a fuller case graph.

claims.statement: VA uses the terms Gulf War illness, chronic multisymptom illness, medically unexplained chronic multisymptom illness, and undiagnosed illness; VA prefers not to use 'Gulf War Syndrome' because reported symptoms vary widely.
claims.perspective: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs public-health guidance

claims.statement: As of the VA page updated July 24, 2026, qualifying Gulf War Veterans may receive presumptive service connection for specified chronic multisymptom or undiagnosed illnesses when current service, location, duration, and other criteria are met; individual eligibility must be checked against current VA rules.
claims.perspective: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs benefits guidance as captured 2026-08-27
claims.uncertainty: Benefits rules and page wording can change; this System never makes an individual eligibility determination.

claims.statement: The VA Gulf War Registry health exam is free to eligible Veterans, does not require VA health-care enrollment, and is separate from a disability compensation exam or claim.
claims.perspective: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs registry guidance

claims.statement: The 2025 National Veteran Suicide Prevention Annual Report, released in 2026 and based on data through 2023, recorded 6,398 Veteran suicide deaths in 2023; the report emphasizes hope, purpose, community, and comprehensive support systems.
claims.perspective: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs national annual report
claims.uncertainty: Population statistics cannot determine any individual's risk and must not be used as a personal score.

claims.statement: Veterans and people concerned about a Veteran can reach confidential Veterans Crisis Line support 24/7 by calling 988 then pressing 1, texting 838255, or using the official chat; emergencies may also require 911 or the nearest emergency department.
claims.perspective: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs crisis guidance as captured 2026-08-27

claims.statement: Vet Center services can include eligible Veterans, service members, and family members when family participation supports the Veteran's or service member's goals; bereavement services can include families affected by suicide.
claims.perspective: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Vet Center eligibility guidance
claims.uncertainty: Eligibility is program-specific and must be checked with the current official service.

claims.statement: The consequences of service continue across Veterans, families, chosen support networks, institutions, bodies, records, work, care, benefits, grief, humor, and memory after formal service ends.
claims.perspective: Mapshifting synthesis grounded in current VA pathways and the Military Systems aftercare module
claims.uncertainty: No single Veteran or family experience is treated as universal.
